intent: Commits: resolve a blocked commit from the Dashboard (#76)
notes: The override command gains a machine-readable mode (`gator hook override status|approve|cancel --json`), so the Dashboard can show and approve a blocked commit without reading Git-private state or parsing terminal text.

Approve and cancel accept `--expect-block` / `--expect-revision` and refuse when the findings or approval changed after the Architect looked; the revision also covers unreadable records, so a damaged block can still be discarded safely.
Status reports which approvable findings an earlier approval already covers and which still need one, from the same rule the hook applies, so a partial approval never looks complete.
The hook dispatcher prints its runtime advisory to stderr for JSON override calls, so their stdout stays one JSON object. Human output is unchanged.

The Dashboard relays that command for one repository (`GET /api/repo/<name>/override`, `POST …/override/approve` and `…/override/cancel`), serving only an allowlisted projection and validating every request before the command runs; posts keep the Dashboard header check and same-repository exclusion, an older runtime degrades to an honest "unsupported" answer, and a block with more findings than the Dashboard can show in full is read-only there (terminal guidance), never silently cut while approvable.

Commits shows a quiet alert while a commit is blocked and opens a dialog that groups the findings as external approval, Architect decision and fix required. Approve appears only for findings that still need an approval, after the name, reason and the existing 10-second delay; every approve or discard re-reads the state first and stops if it changed. Pauses and fix-required findings are explained, never approvable, and nothing implies a commit happened.
